band_change_evidence_test.explanation: Three independent sources at tier 4 or above support the band change. The Singapore Exchange corporate announcement of 14 August 2017 is a regulatory filing (tier 5) and establishes the ownership fact. ST Engineering’s Sustainability Report 2025 and Sustainability Report 2024 are published institutional data (tier 4). Four further independent tier-3 sources — The Record, TechCrunch, CyberScoop and WESA — corroborate the 2022 vulnerability disclosure, the response timeline and the deployment scale, and they were published independently of one another.

key_evidence: Why it matters: the index calls this company "Aethon (Teradyne)". Aethon has been owned by ST Engineering since August 2017 and has never been a Teradyne company. That is an entity-record error, separate from the score.

In April 2022 researchers disclosed five zero-day flaws in Aethon TUG hospital robots, one rated 9.8 out of 10. They allowed remote takeover of robot fleets, access to real-time camera feeds of patients and staff, and disruption of medication delivery, elevators and doors.
Aethon did not find those flaws. A cybersecurity firm hired by one of its hospital customers found them during an audit, and they reached the company through a federal disclosure process.

The response was competent and fast. ST Engineering was told on 6 January 2022, and a patch was tested and confirmed effective on 4 April 2022 and rolled out to all fleets, with firewall help for hospitals. That drives the Action score of 3.0, the highest of Aethon’s eight dimensions.
No repair was made to the patients or staff whose privacy was exposed, and no post-incident architecture review was published.

evidence.claim: ST Engineering’s Land Systems Sector Completes Acquisition of Aethon.
evidence.source: Singapore Exchange — ST Engineering’s Land Systems Sector Completes Acquisition of Aethon Inc (regulatory announcement)

evidence.claim: Aethon entered into an agreement to be acquired by ST Engineering on July 17, 2017. ST Engineering acquired Pittsburgh-based robotics firm Aethon Inc for $36 million. Aethon became a division of ST Engineering’s US headquarters, VT Systems and part of the group’s Land Systems sector.
evidence.source: The Robot Report — ST Engineering acquires mobile robot maker Aethon Inc. for $36 million

evidence.claim: ST Engineering stated they were informed January 6 and took immediate action. "A system patch has been prepared and rolled out to eliminate the possibility of exploitation." The patch was tested and confirmed effective April 4, 2022. The company claimed "no evidence showing the vulnerabilities were exploited."
evidence.source: The Record (Recorded Future News) — Five zero days affecting Aethon hospital autonomous robots patched

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — TWO SEPARATE ISSUES. (1) ENTITY-RECORD-CURRENCY DEFECT: the index lists "Aethon (Teradyne)". Aethon has been owned by ST Engineering since 14 August 2017 and was never a Teradyne company. Teradyne owns Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots. The parenthetical should be corrected regardless of any score decision. (2) SEED CORRECTION: the published 60.9 is a never-assessed uniform placeholder shared byte-for-byte with nine other robotics labs; Aethon has never been individually assessed. Unlike most of the cluster this is not purely an evidence-absence gap — one substantiated adverse event exists, the April 2022 JekyllBot:5 disclosure — but that event is four years old and is scored in both directions, lowering Awareness and Boundaries while raising Action and Accountability. Twenty-three of forty subdimensions still score at the low anchor for absence of disclosure.
